parameters.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a follow-up report containing known causes and corrective actions within 30 days. They must notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident presents a safety risk to their unit or requires customer action. Reports must include incidents regardless of whether injury or damage occurred; suspected incidents must be reported and may be updated as facts are confirmed.

S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a follow-up report containing known causes and corrective actions within 30 days. They must notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident presents a safety risk to their unit or requires customer action. Reports must include incidents regardless of whether injury or damage occurred; suspected incidents must be reported and may be updated as facts are confirmed. Records must be retained for at least 10 years.

S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units. Before sale and after any material design change, manufacturers must submit full results to the regulator, including protocol, sample size, failure count and rate, and testing date. parameters.quote: Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of safety risks, required precautions, and corrective actions, and provide updates as material information becomes available. A recall is mandatory when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. Manufacturers must notify regulators and affected customers without delay upon reaching the trigger, stop sales of the affected model, and implement regulator-approved corrective action or removal.

S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of safety risks, required precautions, and corrective actions, and provide updates as material information becomes available. A recall is mandatory when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. The rate must use the model’s installed-unit count for that same period; incident classifications and unit counts must be supported by records available for regulator audit. Manufacturers must notify regulators and affected customers without delay upon reaching the trigger, stop sales of the affected model, and implement regulator-approved corrective action or removal.

judge_section_notes: The final text lets customers obtain full per-model test results, including failure rates, while public disclosure of per-model rates is excluded, so the S2 red-line compromise held. Both flagships are constrained: the 5% S2 cap forces an immediate sales stop for a model above it, and the 8/100k S5 recall trigger has no transition window. S3's 6-year retrofit and S4's 36-month suppression deadline sit inside the acceptable ranges, and S1 requires 24-hour reporting of all incidents, including suspected ones.
